title: Constrained decoder: backoff & graceful-degradation test matrix for streamed tool calls
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Scope: Build an automated test harness and manual playbook that validates schema adherence when structured outputs are produced in streaming responses and during tool/function calls. This ticket covers constrained-decoder modes (strict/soft), a backoff/graceful-degradation strategy for partial or malformed outputs, and end-to-end compatibility checks across runtime-2.3 variants.

Goals:
- Verify JSON/object schema validity across streaming chunk boundaries and toolcall boundaries.
- Exercise constrained-decoding settings (hard reject, soft-correct, n-best rewrites) and measure trade-offs (validity vs latency).
- Implement + validate a backoff heuristic that emits best-effort structured payloads when strict enforcement fails, and confirm this keeps apps resilient.
- Add mutation-based fuzz and golden prompt sets to catch drift and edge cases.

Test matrix (high level):
- Modes: strict-constrained, soft-constrained, no-constraint baseline.
- Input classes: short single-turn, long prompt with prefix caching, streaming long outputs, nested tool-calls (function return objects), truncated token budget scenarios.
- Failure modes: partial JSON chunks, interleaved toolcall text, invalid types for required fields, extra unknown fields, KV-cache-induced token shifts.
- Load profiles: local dev harness (single worker), CI smoke (10 concurrent sessions), stress (100 concurrent sessions using dedicated-sim harness).

Acceptance criteria:
- Under CI smoke, schema-validity for strict-constrained >= 99.5% on golden prompts.
- Backoff path triggers < 0.5% on golden prompts and provides a documented fallback object with an explicit "fallback_reason" field.
- Latency overhead from constrained decoding (strict mode) <= 5% p50 relative to baseline unless validity gain > 30%.
- Streaming reassembly verifier must reconstruct chunked payloads and detect malformed boundaries with > 99% sensitivity.

Automation & artifacts:
- Add new harness 'hybrid-structured-verifier' in test infra repo: github.com/redwood-inference/test-infra/pulls/237 (WIP).
- Confluence plan + playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Structured+Output+Backoff+Playbook.
- Dashboard: create dashboard tile runtime-2.3 -> structured-output -> validity-rate on Grafana (placeholder link).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: strict enforcement may regress user latency-sensitive workloads. Mitigation: add soft mode and per-route toggles; measure per-route in staging.
- Risk: fuzzing may produce nondeterministic flaky tests. Mitigation: seed corpus + snapshot golden responses.

Implementation notes:
- We'll reuse streaming reassembly logic from ENG-14266 and the fallback semantics described in ENG-45120.
- Backoff algorithm: attempt 2 automated repairs (trim trailing comma, try simple type-coercion for numeric strings), then emit best-effort JSON with fallback_reason and truncated=true if still invalid.
- Tests will assert both the runtime log lines and the returned payload shape.

Next steps:
1) Deliver initial harness and golden prompts (owner: Arjun Patel) by 2026-02-24.
2) Add CI job and run on nightly stress by 2026-03-05.
3) Iterate on backoff heuristics based on results and ship runbook to ENGOncall by 2026-03-15.
